question.text: An investor holding a 10-year bond to maturity faces the highest reinvestment risk when:

answer.text: Interest rates rise during the holding period
Interest rates fall during the holding period
The bond is a zero-coupon bond

explanation.text: The Logic: Reinvestment risk is the risk that coupon receipts during the bond's life are reinvested at lower market rates. When interest rates decrease during the bond's life, coupons are reinvested at progressively lower rates, reducing overall returns for hold-to-maturity investors (NISM-Series-X-A, p.155). The Trap: Rising rates increase reinvestment income but cause capital losses — reinvestment risk specifically refers to the risk of rates falling during the bond's life. Note: STRIPS (zero-coupon bonds) have zero reinvestment risk because there are no intermediate coupons to reinvest (NISM-Series-X-A, p.175).
